issues.message: Diusulkan dilewati: Duplikat: Minotaur (Q129866, artikel en Minotaur) sudah ada di Mythics sebagai slug `minotaur`, diriset lengkap di batch-004. Entri ganda ini tidak diterbitkan. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minotaur).

claims.statement: Nymphs are minor female nature deities or spirits in Greek myth.
claims.statement_id: Nymph adalah dewi kecil atau roh perempuan alam dalam mitologi Yunani.
claims.quote: NYMPHAI (Nymphs) were female spirits of the natural world--minor goddesses of the forests, rivers, springs, meadows, mountains and seas.

claims.statement: Nymphs are depicted as young women with attributes of their habitats.
claims.statement_id: Nymph digambarkan sebagai perempuan muda dengan ciri sesuai tempat tinggalnya.
claims.quote: The nymphs were depicted as beautiful young women with attributes matching their abode.

claims.statement: Nymphs were companions of gods.
claims.statement_id: Nymph dikisahkan sebagai pengiring para dewa.
claims.quote: Nymphs were also companions of the gods.

claims.statement: Some nymphs were said to nurse infant Zeus and Dionysos.
claims.statement_id: Sejumlah Nymph dikisahkan merawat Zeus kecil dan Dionysos.
claims.quote: Others were the nurses of the gods including the Idaian nymphs who nursed the infant Zeus, and the Nysian nymphs who cared for Dionysos.

claims.statement: Ancient Greek nymph types were fluid rather than rigid categories.
claims.statement_id: Jenis-jenis Nymph dalam sumber Yunani kuno tidak memiliki batas yang kaku.
claims.quote: Ancient Greek writers describe many types of nymph but the classifications were rather fluid.

claims.statement: Naiads are freshwater nymphs of springs, rivers, streams, wells, and fountains.
claims.statement_id: Naiad adalah Nymph air tawar yang terkait mata air, sungai, dan sumur.
claims.quote: NAIADES (Naiads) were nymphs of the earthly sources of fresh-water, including springs, rivers, streams, wells and fountains.

claims.statement: Dryads are nymphs of trees and forests.
claims.statement_id: Dryad adalah Nymph pepohonan dan hutan.
claims.quote: DRYADES (Dryads) were the nymphs of the trees, forests and groves.

claims.statement: Oreads are mountain-dwelling nymphs.
claims.statement_id: Oread adalah Nymph yang menghuni pegunungan.
claims.quote: OREIADES (Oreads) were mountain-dwelling nymphs.

claims.statement: Shrines to nymphs have been found in caves in the Greek world.
claims.statement_id: Tempat pemujaan Nymph ditemukan di gua-gua wilayah Yunani.
claims.quote: shrines dedicated to nymphs have been found in caves across the Greek world, such as at Vari on Mount Hymettus

claims.statement: Greek art imagined nymphs dancing in circles outside caves.
claims.statement_id: Nymph dibayangkan menari melingkar di luar gua dalam seni Yunani.
claims.quote: people imagined the Nymphs dancing in circle outside their caves on mount Helicon, in Phocis, in Attica and throughout Greece.

claims.statement: Nymphs also appear in Roman mythology as young nature deities.
claims.statement_id: Nymph juga dikenal dalam mitologi Romawi sebagai dewi muda alam.
claims.quote: A nymph (Greek: νύμφη, nymphē) in Greek and in Roman mythology is a young female deity typically identified with natural features

claims.statement: Hamadryads were Dryad nymphs whose life force was bound to a specific tree.
claims.statement_id: Hamadryad adalah Dryad yang daya hidupnya terikat pada satu pohon tertentu.
claims.quote: HAMADRYADES or HADRYADES (Hamadryads) were Dryad nymphs whose life force was bound to that of a specific tree.

claims.statement: Nymphs of certain springs were thought to have prophetic or oracular power and to inspire men with it and with the gift of poetry.
claims.statement_id: Nymph yang menjaga mata air tertentu dianggap memiliki daya ramal dan dapat mengilhami manusia dengan daya itu serta karunia puisi.
claims.quote: Many of these presided over waters or springs which were believed to inspire those that drank of them, and hence the nymphs themselves were thought to be endowed with prophetic or oracular power, and to inspire men with the same, and to confer upon them the gift of poetry.

claims.statement: Some nymphs were regarded as able to restore sick persons to health.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian nymph dianggap mampu memulihkan orang sakit.
claims.quote: some were thus regarded as having the power of restoring sick persons to health

claims.statement: Nymphs of forests, groves, and glens were believed sometimes to appear to and frighten solitary travellers.
claims.statement_id: Nymph hutan, hutan kecil, dan lembah dipercaya kadang menampakkan diri dan menakuti pelancong yang sendirian.
claims.quote: Nymphs of forests, groves, and glens, were believed sometimes to appear to and frighten solitary travellers.

claims.statement: Tree nymphs were believed to die together with the trees that had been their abode and with which they came into existence.
claims.statement_id: Nymph pepohonan dipercaya mati bersama pohon yang menjadi tempat tinggal dan tempat mereka lahir.
claims.quote: Nymphs of trees, were believed to die together with the trees which had been their abode, and with which they had come into existence.

claims.statement: Sacrifices offered to nymphs usually consisted of goats, lambs, milk, and oil, but never of wine.
claims.statement_id: Persembahan kepada nymph biasanya berupa kambing, domba, susu, dan minyak, tetapi tidak pernah anggur.
claims.quote: The sacrifices offered to nymphs usually consisted of goats, lambs, milk, and oil, but never of wine.

claims.statement: The Okeanides (Oceanids) were the eldest of the nymphs, daughters of the earth-encircling River Okeanos (Oceanus).
claims.statement_id: Okeanid adalah kelompok nymph tertua, putri Sungai Okeanos yang mengelilingi bumi.
claims.quote: OKEANIDES (Oceanids) were the eldest of the nymphs, daughters of the great, earth-encircling River Okeanos (Oceanus).

claims.statement: In modern compilations the Okeanides are often mistakenly described as "ocean" nymphs, but in Greek mythology their father Okeanos was an earth-encircling fresh-water stream and not a salt-sea ocean.
claims.statement_id: Okeanid dalam kumpulan modern sering keliru disebut nymph "samudra", padahal dalam mitologi Yunani ayah mereka, Okeanos, adalah aliran air tawar yang mengelilingi bumi dan bukan samudra air asin.
claims.quote: In modern compilations Okeanides are often mistakenly described as "ocean" nymphs. In Greek mythology, however, their father Okeanos "Ocean" was an earth-encircling, fresh-water stream and not a salt-sea ocean.

claims.statement: Nymphs could also be part of the divine retinue of gods such as Apollo, Dionysos or Pan, or of goddesses such as Artemis, known as the tutelary deity of all nymphs.
claims.statement_id: Nymph juga menjadi bagian rombongan ilahi para dewa seperti Apollo, Dionysos, dan Pan, atau dewi seperti Artemis, yang dikenal sebagai dewi pelindung semua nymph.
claims.quote: or as part of the divine retinue of a comparable god such as Apollo, Dionysos or Pan, or goddesses, such as Artemis, who was known as the tutelary deity of all nymphs.

claims.statement: Like Pan, nymphs in their natural habitat may drive mortals insane or insensate (nympholepsy), particularly at midday.
claims.statement_id: Seperti Pan, nymph di habitat alaminya dapat membuat manusia gila atau tak sadarkan diri (nympholepsy), terutama pada tengah hari.
claims.quote: Like Pan, nymphs within their natural habitat may drive mortals insane or insensate (known as nympholepsy), particularly at midday.

claims.statement: Nymphs are often the mothers of heroes, as in the case of Achilles and Thamyris.
claims.statement_id: Nymph sering menjadi ibu para pahlawan, seperti pada Achilles dan Thamyris.
claims.quote: Nymphs are often the mothers of heroes, as was the case for Achilles and Thamyris

claims.statement: Archaeological evidence suggests that in the archaic period the cult of the nymphs was a primary concern of the rural poor and focused on water sources.
claims.statement_id: Bukti arkeologi menunjukkan bahwa pada periode arkais pemujaan nymph menjadi perhatian utama kaum miskin pedesaan dan berpusat pada sumber air.
claims.quote: Archaeological evidence suggests that the cult of the nymphs in the archaic period was a primary concern of the rural poor, and focused on water sources

claims.statement: In the earliest rural form, anyone passing a fountain-shrine customarily left an offering, typically an animal sacrifice such as a portion of a boar, goat, or sheep.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bentuk pedesaan paling awal, orang yang melewati kuil mata air lazim meninggalkan persembahan, biasanya hewan kurban seperti bagian dari babi hutan, kambing, atau domba.
claims.quote: it was customary for anyone passing a fountain-shrine to leave an offering, typically in the form of an animal sacrifice, such as a portion of a boar, goat, or sheep

claims.statement: The Greek name nymph is translated as "girl of marriageable age".
claims.statement_id: Nama Yunani nymph diterjemahkan sebagai "gadis usia menikah".
claims.quote: Translation Girl of Marriageable Age

claims.statement: Rhea is a female Titan and mother goddess in Greek myth.
claims.statement_id: Rhea adalah Titan perempuan dan dewi ibu dalam mitologi Yunani.
claims.quote: Rhea (also spelt Rheia) is a Titan and a mother goddess in Greek mythology.

claims.statement: Rhea is daughter of Gaia and Uranus and mother of major Olympian deities.
claims.statement_id: Rhea adalah putri Gaia dan Uranus serta ibu para dewa Olimpus.
claims.quote: She is the daughter of Gaia (Earth) and Uranus (Heaven) and the mother of the great deities of Mount Olympus.

claims.statement: Rhea's Roman counterpart was Ops.
claims.statement_id: Padanan Romawi Rhea ialah Ops.
claims.quote: Her Roman counterpart was Ops, a fertility deity and the goddess of the harvest.

claims.statement: Rhea saved Zeus from being swallowed by his father Cronus.
claims.statement_id: Rhea menyelamatkan Zeus agar tidak ditelan ayahnya, Cronus.
claims.quote: Rhea is most well-known as the mother of the Olympian deities, especially Zeus, who she saved from being swallowed by his father, Cronus.

claims.statement: Rhea gave Kronos a swaddled stone instead of infant Zeus.
claims.statement_id: Rhea memberi Kronos batu berbalut kain sebagai pengganti Zeus bayi.
claims.quote: Rhea meanwhile gave Kronos a stone wrapped in the swaddling-cloths to swallow in place of his newborn son.

claims.statement: Infant Zeus was entrusted to the Kouretes and nymphs Adrasteia and Ide.
claims.statement_id: Zeus kecil dipercayakan kepada Kouretes dan dua Nymph bernama Adrasteia dan Ide.
claims.quote: She put him in the care of both the Kouretes (Curetes) and the Nymphai (Nymphs) Adrasteia and Ide (Ida)

claims.statement: The Kouretes clashed shields to hide infant Zeus's cries from Cronus.
claims.statement_id: Kouretes membenturkan perisai untuk menutupi tangis Zeus dari Cronus.
claims.quote: They sang and danced and clashed their shields to drown out the cries of the infant Zeus and protect him from his father.

claims.statement: Rhea became closely associated with the Phrygian goddess Cybele.
claims.statement_id: Rhea kemudian dikaitkan dengan dewi Frigia Cybele.
claims.quote: Rhea was closely associated with Cybele, a Phrygian goddess who was worshipped across Greece, Rome and Anatolia.

claims.statement: Rhea and Cybele began as separate figures before being identified.
claims.statement_id: Rhea dan Cybele mula-mula merupakan identitas terpisah sebelum dipadankan.
claims.quote: Rhea and Cybele began as two separate identities, but they essentially became two manifestations of the same deity.

claims.statement: The Metroön at Olympia honored Rhea as mother of the gods.
claims.statement_id: Kuil Metroön di Olympia didedikasikan bagi Rhea sebagai ibu para dewa.
claims.quote: In Olympia, there was a temple known as the Metroön, which was built for Rhea in honour of her role as mother of the gods.

claims.statement: Diodorus names Hestia, Demeter, Hera, Zeus, Poseidon, and Hades as Rhea's children.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Diodorus menyebut Hestia, Demeter, Hera, Zeus, Poseidon, dan Hades sebagai anak Rhea.
claims.quote: To Kronos (Cronus) and Rhea, we are told, were born Hestia, Demeter, and Hera, and Zeus, Poseidon, and Haides

claims.statement: Rhea, like Demeter, was a goddess of the earth.
claims.statement_id: Rhea, seperti Demeter, adalah dewi bumi.
claims.quote: but thus much seems undeniable, that Rhea, like Demeter, was a goddess of the earth.

claims.statement: Cronos is said to have devoured all his children by Rhea, but when she was about to give birth to Zeus she went, on her parents' advice, to Lyctus in Crete.
claims.statement_id: Cronos dikisahkan menelan semua anaknya dari Rhea, tetapi ketika Rhea hampir melahirkan Zeus, atas saran orang tuanya ia pergi ke Lyctus di Kreta.
claims.quote: Cronos is said to have devoured all his children by Rhea, but when she was on the point of giving birth to Zeus, she, by the advice of her parents, went to Lyctus in Crete.

claims.statement: At Delphi there was a smallish stone anointed with oil every day and wrapped in white wool on solemn occasions; it was believed to be the stone Cronos swallowed when he thought he was devouring Zeus.
claims.statement_id: Di Delphi ada sebuah batu kecil yang diurapi minyak setiap hari dan dibungkus wol putih pada upacara khidmat; batu itu dipercaya sebagai batu yang ditelan Cronos ketika ia mengira sedang menelan Zeus.
claims.quote: At Delphi there was a stone of not very large dimensions, which was every day anointed with oil, and on solemn occasions was wrapped up in white wool; and this stone was believed to have been the one which Cronos swallowed when he thought he was devouring Zeus

claims.statement: Rhea is designated by various names, including "the great mother," "the mother of the gods," Cybele, Cybebe, Agdistis, Berecyntia, Brimo, and Dindymene.
claims.statement_id: Rhea disebut dengan berbagai nama, antara lain "ibu agung", "ibu para dewa", Cybele, Cybebe, Agdistis, Berecyntia, Brimo, dan Dindymene.
claims.quote: The various names by which we find Rhea designated, are, "the great mother," "the mother of the gods," Cybele, Cybebe, Agdistis, Berecyntia, Brimo, Dindymene, "the great Idaean mother of the gods."

claims.statement: The Corybantes were her enthusiastic priests, who with drums, cymbals, horns, and in full armour performed orgiastic dances in the forests and on the mountains of Phrygia.
claims.statement_id: Para Corybantes adalah imam-imamnya yang antusias, yang menarikan tarian orgiastik dengan genderang, simbal, dan tanduk serta berbaju zirah lengkap di hutan dan pegunungan Frigia.
claims.quote: The Corybantes were her enthusiastic priests, who with drums, cymbals, horns, and in full armour, performed their orgiastic dances in the forests and on the mountains of Phrygia.

claims.statement: In Greece the oak was sacred to Rhea.
claims.statement_id: Di Yunani, pohon ek keramat bagi Rhea.
claims.quote: In Greece the oak was sacred to Rhea

claims.statement: The lion was sacred to the mother of the gods, because she was the divinity of the earth.
claims.statement_id: Singa keramat bagi ibu para dewa, karena ia adalah dewata bumi.
claims.quote: The lion was sacred to the mother of the gods, because she was the divinity of the earth

claims.statement: Crete was undoubtedly the earliest seat of the worship of Rhea.
claims.statement_id: Kreta tidak diragukan lagi merupakan pusat pemujaan Rhea yang paling awal.
claims.quote: Crete was undoubtedly the earliest seat of the worship of Rhea

claims.statement: According to some accounts Cronos and Rhea were preceded in sovereignty over the world by Ophion and Eurynome; Ophion was overpowered by Cronos, and Rhea cast Eurynome into Tartarus.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebagian kisah, Cronos dan Rhea didahului dalam kekuasaan atas dunia oleh Ophion dan Eurynome; Ophion dikalahkan Cronos, dan Rhea melempar Eurynome ke Tartarus.
claims.quote: According to some accounts Cronos and Rhea were preceded in their sovereignty over the world by Ophion and Eurynome ; but Ophion was overpowered by Cronos, and Rhea cast Eurynome into Tartarus.

claims.statement: She was seldom represented standing, but generally seated on a throne, wearing the mural crown with a veil hanging down; lions usually appear crouching to the right and left of her throne.
claims.statement_id: Rhea jarang digambarkan berdiri, umumnya duduk di singgasana dengan mahkota tembok dan cadar menjuntai; singa biasanya berjongkok di kanan dan kiri singgasananya.
claims.quote: she was seldom represented in a standing posture, but generally seated on a throne, adorned with the mural crown, from which a veil hangs down. Lions usually appear crouching on the right and left of her throne

claims.statement: The name Rhea is translated as "flow, ease".
claims.statement_id: Nama Rhea diterjemahkan sebagai "aliran, kemudahan".
claims.quote: Rhea Translation Flow, Ease (rhea)

claims.statement: In Hyginus (Preface), Rhea's parents are Aither (or Ouranos) and Gaia.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Hyginus (Pref), orang tua Rhea adalah Aither (atau Ouranos) dan Gaia.
claims.quote: [1.2] AITHER (or OURANOS) & GAIA (Hyginus Pref)

claims.statement: In Homer, Iliad 15.187, Rhea's children by Kronos are Zeus, Poseidon, and Haides.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Homer, Iliad 15.187, anak Rhea dari Kronos adalah Zeus, Poseidon, dan Hades.
claims.quote: [1.2] ZEUS, POSEIDON, HAIDES (by Kronos) (Homer Iliad 15.187)

claims.statement: In Homeric Hymn 2.69, Rhea's children are Zeus, Demeter, and Haides.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Homeric Hymn 2.69, anak Rhea adalah Zeus, Demeter, dan Hades.
claims.quote: [1.3] ZEUS, DEMETER, HAIDES (Homeric Hymn 2.69)

claims.statement: In a classical source, he wedded his sister Rhea, and since Earth and Sky foretold he would be dethroned by his own son, he swallowed his offspring at birth: Hestia, then Demeter and Hera, then Pluto and Poseidon.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebuah sumber klasik, ia menikahi saudarinya Rhea, dan karena Bumi dan Langit meramalkan ia akan digulingkan putranya sendiri, ia menelan anak-anaknya saat lahir: Hestia, lalu Demeter dan Hera, kemudian Pluto dan Poseidon.
claims.quote: wedded his sister Rhea; and since both Earth and Sky foretold him that he would be dethroned by his own son, he used to swallow his offspring at birth. His firstborn Hestia he swallowed, then Demeter and Hera, and after them Pluto and Poseidon.

claims.statement: In a classical source, Rhea went to Crete when big with Zeus and brought him forth in a cave of Dicte.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebuah sumber klasik, Rhea pergi ke Kreta ketika mengandung Zeus dan melahirkannya di sebuah gua di Dicte.
claims.quote: Rhea repaired to Crete, when she was big with Zeus, and brought him forth in a cave of Dicte.

claims.statement: The ancients were not agreed whether the infant god had been reared on Mount Ida or Mount Dicte.
claims.statement_id: Orang-orang kuno tidak sepakat apakah dewa bayi itu dibesarkan di Gunung Ida atau Gunung Dicte.
claims.quote: The ancients were not agreed as to whether the infant god had been reared on Mount Ida or Mount Dicte.

claims.statement: Homer makes only a passing allusion to Rhea, so the passage of Hesiod must be regarded as the most ancient Greek legend about Rhea.
claims.statement_id: Homer hanya menyinggung Rhea sekilas, sehingga bagian dalam Hesiod harus dianggap sebagai legenda Yunani tertua tentang Rhea.
claims.quote: Homer (Il. xv. 187) makes only a passing allusion to Rhea, and the passage of Hesiod, which accordingly must be regarded as the most ancient Greek legend about Rhea

claims.statement: Vulcan is the Roman god of fire and forge, equivalent to Greek Hephaestus.
claims.statement_id: Vulcan adalah dewa api dan penempaan Romawi, dipadankan dengan Hephaestus Yunani.
claims.quote: Vulcan or Volcanus was the Roman god of fire and forge, the equivalent of Hephaestus from Greek mythology.

claims.statement: Vulcan is the son of Jupiter and Juno and patron of smiths and artisans.
claims.statement_id: Vulcan adalah putra Jupiter dan Juno serta pelindung pandai besi dan perajin.
claims.quote: The son of Jupiter and Juno, he was the special patron of blacksmiths and artisans.

claims.statement: The Vulcanalia festival was celebrated on 23 August.
claims.statement_id: Festival Vulcanalia diperingati pada 23 Agustus.
claims.quote: Vulcan had a festival, the Vulcanalia (the Hephaestia) celebrated on 23 August

claims.statement: A temple of Vulcan stood on the Campus Martius outside Rome.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kuil Vulcan terletak di Campus Martius di luar Roma.
claims.quote: a temple located outside Rome on the Campus Martius.

claims.statement: In a Roman account Vulcan established a forge at Mount Aetna with Cyclopes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Romawi, Vulcan menempa di Gunung Aetna bersama para Cyclopes.
claims.quote: According to the Roman account, Vulcan withdrew to Mount Aetna where he established a great forge and partnered with the Cyclopes Bronte, Steropes, and Pyraemon.

claims.statement: Vulcan made a trapped golden throne for Juno.
claims.statement_id: Vulcan membuat takhta emas berperangkap untuk Juno.
claims.quote: Vulcan fashioned a beautiful golden throne for Juno, but it contained a number of hidden springs.

claims.statement: In a Roman myth Vulcan opens Jupiter's head and Minerva emerges.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebuah mitos Romawi, Vulcan membuka kepala Jupiter hingga Minerva lahir.
claims.quote: Finally, Jupiter appealed to Vulcan to open up his head with an axe. Vulcan quickly complied, and Minerva sprang forth, fully grown and clad in her armor.

claims.statement: In the Aeneid Venus asks Vulcan to forge arms for Aeneas.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Aeneid, Venus meminta Vulcan membuat senjata dan zirah bagi Aeneas.
claims.quote: Venus is concerned for her son Aeneas' safety and appeals to her husband Vulcan to make him weapons and armor.

claims.statement: Renaissance art often depicts Vulcan as a lame blacksmith.
claims.statement_id: Seni Renaisans sering menampilkan Vulcan sebagai pandai besi yang pincang.
claims.quote: In Renaissance art, the Roman god of fire is usually shown in the character of a crippled blacksmith.

claims.statement: Vulcan was regarded as patron of workers with molten metal.
claims.statement_id: Vulcan juga dipandang sebagai pelindung pekerja logam cair.
claims.quote: As patron of those who worked with molten metal, Vulcan must have had a special meaning for the bronze artist.

claims.statement: Angry with his son's interference, Jupiter threw him out of heaven; Vulcan fell for a full day and night, landing on the summit of Mount Mosychulus on Lemnos, and the fall left him lame and deformed.
claims.statement_id: Marah pada campur tangan putranya, Jupiter melemparkannya dari surga; Vulcan jatuh sehari semalam dan mendarat di puncak Gunung Mosychulus di pulau Lemnos, dan jatuhnya itu membuatnya pincang dan cacat.
claims.quote: Angry with his son's interference, Jupiter threw him out of heaven. Vulcan fell to earth for one full day and night, landing on the summit of Mount Mosychulus on the island of Lemnos. The severity of the fall left him lame and deformed

claims.statement: As a punishment to Venus for her pride and rejection of all suitors, Jupiter married the goddess of beauty to the "ill-favored" Vulcan.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai hukuman bagi Venus atas kesombongannya dan penolakannya terhadap semua pelamar, Jupiter menikahkan dewi kecantikan itu dengan Vulcan yang "buruk rupa".
claims.quote: as a punishment to Venus for her pride and rejection of all suitors, Jupiter married the goddess of beauty to the 'ill-favored' Vulcan

claims.statement: The marriage did not last, and Venus left him for the affection of others, one of them being his brother Mars.
claims.statement_id: Pernikahan itu tidak bertahan; Venus meninggalkannya demi kasih sayang pihak lain, salah satunya Mars, saudara Vulcan.
claims.quote: as a punishment to Venus for her pride and rejection of all suitors, Jupiter married the goddess of beauty to the 'ill-favored' Vulcan, forcing her and her attendants – the Graces – to live with him in his cave in Mount Aetna. Of course, the marriage did not last, and she left him for the affection of others – one of them being his brother Mars.

claims.statement: Vulcan had children, all considered monsters, among them Cacus (slain by Hercules), Periphetes (killed by Theseus), and the wrestler Cercyon.
claims.statement_id: Vulcan memiliki anak-anak yang semuanya dianggap monster, antara lain Cacus (dibunuh Hercules), Periphetes (dibunuh Theseus), dan pegulat Cercyon.
claims.quote: He did, however, have children (all of whom were considered monsters): among them were Cacus (slain by Hercules), Periphetes (killed by Theseus), and the wrestler Cercyon

claims.statement: Bacchus (Dionysus) appealed to Vulcan with a flask of wine; Vulcan consented to free his mother, then returned to his forge and built magnificent palaces for each of the gods.
claims.statement_id: Bacchus (Dionysus) membujuk Vulcan dengan sebotol anggur; Vulcan setuju membebaskan ibunya, lalu kembali ke bengkelnya dan membangun istana megah bagi setiap dewa.
claims.quote: Finally, Bacchus (Dionysus), the god of wine and revelry, appealed to Vulcan's better nature with a flask of wine. Vulcan consented and freed his mother. Afterwards, he returned to his forge and built magnificent palaces for each of the gods.

claims.statement: As god of the forge and of the devastating fire of environment and nature (volcanoes), Vulcan was probably among the most dreaded of all the gods.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai dewa tempa dan api yang menghancurkan di lingkungan dan alam (gunung berapi), Vulcan mungkin termasuk dewa yang paling ditakuti.
claims.quote: As the god of the forge and the devastating fire of both the environment and nature (volcanoes), Vulcan was probably among the most dreaded of all the gods.

claims.statement: For fear of fire and for safety, most of his temples were located outside a city.
claims.statement_id: Karena takut api dan demi keselamatan, sebagian besar kuilnya dibangun di luar kota.
claims.quote: For fear of fire (and for safety), most of his temples were located outside a city.

claims.statement: Vulcan returned to his forge where the Cyclopes were working on Jupiter's thunderbolts and Mars' chariot.
claims.statement_id: Vulcan kembali ke bengkelnya tempat para Cyclopes mengerjakan petir Jupiter dan kereta Mars.
claims.quote: Vulcan returned to his forge where the Cyclopes were working on Jupiter's thunderbolts and Mars' chariot.

claims.statement: On Aeneas' shield, being prophetic, future events of Roman history were portrayed.
claims.statement_id: Pada perisai Aeneas digambarkan peristiwa-peristiwa masa depan sejarah Romawi.
claims.quote: However, on Aeneas' shield (being prophetic) he portrayed future events of Roman history.

claims.statement: Vulcan's ugliness and deformity prevented him from finding happiness in marriage.
claims.statement_id: Keburukan rupa dan cacat tubuh Vulcan menghalanginya menemukan kebahagiaan dalam pernikahan.
claims.quote: Vulcan's ugliness and deformity prevented him from finding happiness in marriage.

claims.statement: After being told of the shame of Venus and Mars, Vulcan's mind reeled and his work fell from his hands; the god of the forge then fashioned a very thin net of fine bronze links and spread it over a couch.
claims.statement_id: Setelah diberi tahu tentang aib Venus dan Mars, pikiran Vulcan terguncang dan pekerjaannya jatuh dari tangannya; dewa tempa itu lalu membuat jaring tipis dari mata rantai perunggu dan membentangkannya di atas ranjang.
claims.quote: was the first to see the shame of Venus and Mars ... He relates what he had seen to Vulcan. ... Vulcan's mind reeled and the work upon which he was engaged fell from his hands ... The god of the forge fashioned a very thin net of fine links of bronze and spread it over a couch.

claims.statement: In the Greek variation, at Hephaestus' birth Hera found him small, swarthy, and ugly and, disgusted, hurled him down the mountainside into the sea.
claims.statement_id: Dalam variasi Yunani, saat Hephaestus lahir, Hera mendapatinya kecil, gelap, dan buruk rupa, lalu dengan jijik melemparkannya menuruni gunung hingga lenyap ke laut.
claims.quote: A variation of this fall comes from Greek mythology. Hera was well aware of Zeus' wandering eye and wanted to give him a child of great strength and power, but at Hephaestus' birth, Hera found him small, swarthy, and ugly. Disgusted, she hurled him down the mountainside, disappearing into the sea.

claims.statement: Vulcan has no planet named for him, only the process of hardening rubber: vulcanization.
claims.statement_id: Vulcan tidak memiliki planet yang dinamai dengannya, hanya proses pengerasan karet: vulkanisasi.
claims.quote: Unfortunately, Vulcan has no planet named for him, only the process of hardening rubber: vulcanization.

claims.statement: Translator's note: cast down from heaven for his deformity, Vulcan fell upon the Isle of Lemnos.
claims.statement_id: Catatan penerjemah: karena dilemparkan dari surga akibat cacat tubuhnya, Vulcan jatuh di Pulau Lemnos.
claims.quote: Being precipitated from heaven for his deformity, Vulcan fell upon the Isle of Lemnos

claims.statement: Vulcan is called "Junonigena" because, according to some, he was the son of Juno alone; other writers say he was the only son of Jupiter and Juno.
claims.statement_id: Vulcan disebut "Junonigena" karena menurut sebagian orang ia putra Juno saja; penulis lain mengatakan ia satu-satunya putra Jupiter dan Juno.
claims.quote: Vulcan is called 'Junonigena,' because, according to some, he was the son of Juno alone. Other writers, however, say that he was the only son of Jupiter and Juno.

claims.statement: The poets say the dog was made by Vulcan and presented by him to Jupiter, who gave it to Europa.
claims.statement_id: Para penyair menyebut anjing itu dibuat oleh Vulcan dan dipersembahkannya kepada Jupiter, yang memberikannya kepada Europa.
claims.quote: The poets tell us, that this dog was made by Vulcan, and presented by him to Jupiter, who gave him to Europa

claims.statement: A lofty chariot with a golden axle-tree and golden poles is called the gift of Vulcan.
claims.statement_id: Kereta tinggi dengan poros dan tiang dari emas disebut sebagai hadiah dari Vulcan.
claims.quote: leads the young man to the lofty chariot, the gift of Vulcan. The axle-tree was of gold, the poles were of gold
